newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B share index ends 10 pct limit-up.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B share index ends 10 pct limit-up.

text.p: Shenzhen's share indices surged on Wednesday after two days of plunges with investors recovering from the shock of the central government's crackdown on the stock markets this week, traders said.
The B share index closed 10-percent limit-up at 133.8 points and the A share index gained 4.37 percent to 391.92 points.
The turnover of B shares jumped to HK$303.77 million from Tuesday's HK$133.63 million.

"Active buying emerged in the early afternoon, with an increasing number of investors reluctant to reduce their B share holdings after the nosedives of the past couple of days," a broker with Shanghai Guotai Securities said.
"Institutional buying targeted shares of firms with strong earnings records," he added.
A harshly-worded commentary in the People's Daily on Monday said that China's stock markets were overheated and warned that if there was a crash, Beijing would not step in to support the market.
The B shares ended at limit-down on Monday and Tuesday due to Beijing's crackdown.
Brokers said today's advances in China's two B share markets were fueled by institutional bargain hunting in shares of firms with strong earnings records.

Comments by the heads of the Shenzhen and Shanghai stock exchanges on Beijing's stock crackdown published on the front of China's main securities newspaper contributed to stabilising market sentiment, analysts said.
"Confidence has recovered slightly because of Wednesday's strong rebounds, but it is still unclear whether the upward momentum will be maintained in the next few sessions," an analyst said.
"Trading will be volatile in the short term," he added.
The A share market was still pressured by selling of cheap and small shares, brokers said. The trading volume of A shares rose to 9.07 billion yuan from 2.78 billion yuan on Wednesday.
